tier: Residential VPS, 2 to 8 core, US Los Angeles (AT&T network, Cox or Astound double-ISP option)

free_tier.stated: No free tier. A trade site's 2025-10-22 reading of the vendor's offer lists four residential plans on a 10 Gbps port with one IPv4: 2 core, 2 GB, 40 GB NVMe, 5 TB a month at 15 USD a month; 4 core, 4 GB, 80 GB, 10 TB at 35 USD; 8 core, 8 GB, 160 GB, 20 TB at 75 USD; 8 core, 16 GB, 320 GB, 40 TB at 155 USD. The default network is a single-ISP AT&T line and 5 USD more selects a Cox Residential or Astound double-ISP address.
free_tier.notes: unverified on the vendor's own pages: the vendor's home page at sixtynet.net renders no plan or price text, and its residential page paths returned 404. The figures are the trade site's reading dated 2025-10-22.

retention.stated: not applicable: a rented machine and its address, not stored bytes

egress.terms: A monthly allowance of 5 TB, 10 TB, 20 TB or 40 TB by plan on a 10 Gbps port, per the trade site's reading. No overage price was read.
egress.free_allowance: 5 TB per month on the 15 USD plan, per a trade site's reading

interface_detail: A KVM virtual machine with one IPv4 (the vendor's FAQ states KVM virtualization and a free 24/7 ticket support). The access method for the residential line is not stated on the pages read.
tooling: An SSH or RDP client plus a proxy or tunnel daemon the user installs on the machine. The vendor publishes no proxy endpoint on the pages read.
chaining: A Worker opens an outbound connection to the machine's IPv4 and the machine makes the upstream request, so the upstream sees an address on the AT&T, Cox or Astound network the plan names instead of AS13335. The trade site says the residential line does not open ports 80 and 443 and blocks ping.

limits.value: 5 TB per month on the 15 USD plan, up to 40 TB on the 155 USD plan, per a trade site

limits_note: The address class is the live question. The trade site's own postscript says readers report the addresses are no longer AT&T residential, and a forum review list says the vendor lost its residential property after an ASN change. The vendor's home page names a single region, US East (Los Angeles).
binding_note: No byte limit binds a low-volume exit. What decides the record is whether the addresses are still residential, and the vendor's pages do not say.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: the sign-up and checkout pages were not read. The kind records an email as the floor.

reliability_note: A trade site warns readers to check with the vendor before buying because some say the addresses are no longer AT&T residential. A forum review list marks the vendor as formerly the best value, with its residential property lost after an ASN change.
confidence_note: Reported. Prices and plan rows come from one trade-site post dated 2025-10-22, the residential property is contested by two third-party sources, and the vendor's own pages gave no plan text. Nothing was measured and no test address is published.
